Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Bank of Botswana has statutory authority under the National Clearance and Settlement Systems (NCSS) Act to “recognise, operate, regulate and supervise payment systems” ([Bank of Botswana – NPS Oversight Policy 2019](https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/sites/default/files/National%20Payments%20System%20Oversight%20Policy%20%202019.pdf)). It also directly manages and operates BISS as settlement provider ([Bank of Botswana – BISS](https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/content/botswana-interbank-settlement-system)).

revised_comments: The Bank of Botswana directly operates Botswana's core payment and settlement infrastructure beyond a purely regulatory role. Under the National Clearance and Settlement Systems Act (Cap. 46:06) and the National Payments System Oversight Policy, the Bank manages and operates the Botswana Interbank Settlement System (BISS), the country's real-time gross settlement system, as well as the Botswana Automated Clearing House (BACH). The Bank's 2024 Banking Supervision Annual Report confirms continued direct operation of both systems, with BISS settlement value rising 38.6% to P1.57 trillion in 2024, and describes an ongoing Bank-led project to develop a national retail payments switch to enhance interoperability.
